questions.q: What is Vermiculture farming?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Vermiculture is the science of raising worms. Earthworm is called 'friend of farmers' and' intestine of the soil'. Earthworm manure or vermicompost is an excellent bio-fertilizer rich in nutrients.

questions.q: The book, The Origin of Species was written by -
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The book ‘On the Origin of Species’ was written by Charles Darwin. Charles Darwin was an English naturalist and biologist. The theory of evolution presented by him is called Darwinism or the Theory of Natural Selection.

questions.q: The reason for large-scale diversity among the organisms is –
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: The group of scientists who gave a modern form to the theory of natural selection is called “Neo-Darwinists”. According to modern Neo-Darwinists, new organisms are formed after small changes in genes, due to which diversity increases in organisms. These changes are called “mutations”. Therefore, the main reason for very high diversity in living organisms is mutation.

questions.q: According to recent proof, the life on earth emerged approximately -
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: According to the modern concept, the origin of life on the Earth occurred about 2,000 million (2,000,000,000) years ago. However, the oldest fossils are about 3,600 million years old. Important early fossils are considered to be remains of stromatolites (Stromatolites), which were a group of unicellular organisms. About 2,000 million years ago, eukaryotic cells originated, from which all living organisms of the present living world (except bacteria) were formed.

questions.q: Latest ancestor of modern human is
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Cro-Magnon man anatomically similar to modern humans. He lived in the Stone Age and used bone tools. He had the ability to stitch and wear animal skins. He lived in caves, and his wall paintings are found on cave walls. He is the most recent prehistoric human.

questions.q: The main factor of development is -
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Today, the most accepted theory of evolution is known as the Modern Synthetic Theory of Evolution. In it, the origin (emergence) of species is explained on the basis of interactions of genetic variations and natural selection. In the process of natural selection, the beneficial traits of welladapted organisms are inherited by the next generations, as a result species gradually change over time.

questions.q: The reason for development is -
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: The most accepted theory of evolution is the Synthetic Theory of Evolution. In it, the origin of species can be understood on the basis of interactions of genetic variations and natural selection; that is, adaptation from generation to generation is the cause of evolution.

questions.q: Protista group includes–

questions.explanation: All unicellular eukaryotic organisms are included in the Protista group. Heterotrophic eukaryotic organisms are included in the Animal Kingdom, and all green plants are included in the Plant Kingdom.

questions.q: In lichen, a chlorophyll-containing partner, __________ live together.
questions.question_type: Fill in the Blank — Single Correct

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In lichens, a chlorophyll-containing partner—algae (phycobiont)—and a chlorophyll-lacking partner—fungus (mycobiont)—live together. This is called mutualism. In this type of association, the fungus is the more dominant partner. The fungus provides shelter, water, and minerals to the algae, and in return, the algae provides food to the fungus, which it prepares through photosynthesis. In lichens, reproduction occurs through the fungal component. In biology, when two organisms help each other, it is called a symbiotic (Mutualism) relationship.

questions.q: In mycorrhizal association, the advantage of plant is :
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.D: Increased mineral absorption and disease protection

questions.explanation: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association formed between certain fungi and the roots of higher plants. In this association, the plant especially benefits through increased absorption of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other micronutrients. Plants with mycorrhiza also get protection from root-borne diseases and some harmful soil microorganisms.

questions.q: Spirogyra is an example of which of the following algae?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Spirogyra is an example of green algae. It contains chlorophyll; therefore, it makes its own food through photosynthesis. There are more than 400 species of Spirogyra worldwide. Spirogyra is also called water silk.

questions.explanation: Diatoms are unicellular algae. They are organisms found on Earth that have a cell wall made of transparent, opaline silica. They belong to the kingdom Protista.

questions.q: Which of the following is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Phylum Arthropoda is the largest phylum of the animal kingdom. Among all species found on Earth, nearly twothirds of the species belong to Arthropoda.

questions.explanation: Phylum Echinodermata: They are exclusively marine organisms. They are multicellular animals with welldeveloped organ systems. Most echinoderms are star-shaped and have a cylindrical body form. They are triploblastic and possess a coelomic cavity. They also have a characteristic water vascular system. They respire through tube feet and dermal bronchiae (skin gills).

questions.q: How do the members of honey-bee hive recognise eachother?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Almost all animals have methods of exchanging information. They communicate through sight, sound, touch and smell. Honeybees perform different dance patterns to indicate the direction of food and the location of its source, while they recognize each other by smell. These smell-based chemicals are pheromones.

questions.q: Dolphins are classified as –

questions.q: Frogs and toads are examples of which of the following amphibians?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Frog and toad are examples of amphibians of the order Anura. Major features of Anura include: they have four limbs; their hind limbs are longer and stronger than the forelimbs, which helps them in jumping.

questions.explanation: In bryophytes, the spore mother cell is diploid. Bryophytes include mosses and liverworts, which are generally found in moist and shady regions of hilly areas. Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom.

questions.q: What is the structural and functional unit of life?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: All living organisms are made up of cells. Some organisms are made of a single cell; they are called unicellular organisms, such as protozoa, Euglena, etc. Organisms like humans, which are made up of many cells, are called multicellular organisms. A unicellular organism can exist independently and perform essential life processes. Anything smaller than a cell cannot ensure independent existence; therefore, the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living beings.

questions.q: The powerhouse of the cell is -
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Mitochondria are double-membrane-bound organelles scattered in the cytoplasm of all living plant and animal cells, except bacteria and blue-green algae (cyanobacteria). They are called the powerhouse of the cell because complete oxidation of glucose takes place in them. Hence, mitochondria are the power source of the cell.

questions.explanation: The word “virus” is derived from the Latin word “virus”, which literally means poison or sticky liquid. Viruses are acellular, ultramicroscopic organisms that can multiply only inside a living cell. Generally, enzymes are absent in viruses; however, some viruses such as retroviruses contain certain enzymes. Chemically, a virus is a segment of nucleic acid surrounded by a protein coat. Outside the host cell, viruses can neither perform any biological activity nor replicate. Enzymes are also present in lichen, bacteria, and algae.

questions.explanation: Plant cells have a cell wall along with a cell membrane. In plants, the cell wall surrounds the cell membrane. It gives a definite shape to the plant cell. Animal cells have a cell membrane, but they do not have a cell wall.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-sense codon?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: In Genetics, a three-nucleotide sequence of mRNA is called a codon. Codons are of two types— Sense codons: These are codons for amino acids and are responsible for protein formation. Their total number is 61. Nonsense (stop) codons: These indicate the termination of protein synthesis. In the standard genetic code, three major stop (nonsense) codons are accepted. These give the termination signal for protein synthesis— UAA (ochre), UAG (amber), and UGA (opal) Therefore, among the given options, only UAA is a nonsense (stop) codon. The remaining are sense codons.

questions.q: Who discovered DNA?

Actually, DNA was first identified in 1869 by the Swiss chemist Friedrich Miescher. Friedrich called it “nuclein.”

questions.q: Advancement occurs through the use of pesticides in terms of:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: By using fertilizers and pesticides, more crops and plants can be produced on less land. They help increase crop productivity. Pesticides also help maximize the benefits of other agricultural inputs such as water resources, fertilizers, and high-quality seeds.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect about muscles in human body?

options.A: Muscles can only push the bone.
options.C: Muscles become shorter, stiffer and thicker when contracted.

options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Muscles help a person in activities such as walking, speaking, eating, etc. They assist in heartbeat, respiration, and digestion. questions.q: Muscle contains contractile proteins -
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Contractile proteins are involved in muscle contraction. Actin (thin filament) and myosin (thick filament) are the contractile proteins in muscles.

questions.q: In which organ of the human body is epithelial cells found?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue is a thin and smooth membrane that covers the outer surfaces of all internal organs of the body. Epithelial tissue is found in various organs/parts of the body such as the tongue, kidney tubules, salivary glands, sweat glands, pancreas, lungs, nose, eyes, and ears.

questions.q: Glycogen stored in liver and muscles of the human body is in form of–
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Glycogen stored in the liver and muscles of the human body is a polysaccharide. Polysaccharides are carbohydrates available in abundance in food. When the body does not obtain sufficient energy from food, the body’s energy supply is met by converting stored glycogen into glucose.

questions.q: The number of bones in the hands and feet of an adult human, compared to the total number of bones in a human, is approximately what percentage?

questions.explanation: In an adult human, the total number of bones is 206, whereas the upper and lower limbs (extremities), i. e., the hands and feet, along with the girdles that connect them to the trunk, together have 126 bones; that is, about 60% of the total bones. questions.q: How many pairs of nerves arise from the spinal cord?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Quantitative Factual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: 31 pairs of nerves arise from the spinal cord, whereas the number of cranial nerves is 12 pairs.

questions.q: The number of teeth that are developed twice in the lifetime of a human being is –
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: In a human’s lifetime, 20 teeth develop twice, and 12 teeth develop only once.

questions.explanation: From morphological and anatomical studies of organisms, we get knowledge about vestigial organs. A vestigial organ appears functionless, but it can be shown to be homologous to an organ that was functional in ancestors. For example, the vermiform appendix in the large intestine of humans, the nictitating membrane of the eye, and the auricular muscles of the pinna. Incisors are not vestigial organs.

questions.q: Stapedius is a–

questions.explanation: Stapedius is the smallest muscle in the human body, located in the ears. It helps stabilize the stapes bone. It controls sound and protects the inner ear from damage due to loud noise.

questions.q: In the human system, insulin controls the metabolism of :
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

questions.explanation: Insulin is produced by the pancreas. It is a hormone (a protein) that plays a major role in regulating glucose homeostasis. Insulin also stimulates the process of converting glucose into glycogen in target cells. Glucose is a form of carbohydrate.

questions.q: Energy is stored in liver and muscles in the form of :
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: The cells of the body need energy to work. This energy is obtained from the chemical reactions of sugar, fat, and protein. In the liver and muscles, energy (glucose) is mainly stored in the form of glycogen.

questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is secreted by the parietal/oxyntic cells present in the stomach. It helps in the digestion of food, but if the acid is present in excess in the stomach, indigestion may occur. To get relief from indigestion, we take an antacid such as milk of magnesia, which contains magnesium hydroxide. It neutralizes the effect of excess acid.

questions.q: The sensitive area of the human tongue to bitterness is:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above

questions.q: Which part of alimentary canal receives bile from the liver ?

questions.explanation: The liver is the largest gland of the human body. It is located just below the diaphragm, connected with the mesentery, and is deep reddish-brown in colour. questions.q: Which of the following is not an endocrine gland?

questions.explanation: The lacrimal gland (tear gland) is not an endocrine gland. These glands are located above each eyeball, due to which tears are secreted in each eye. questions.question_type: List and Code — Incorrect/Exception Combination

questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

questions.q: Substances which are responsible for catalyzing chemical reactions in living systems are -
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts. They are generally proteins and, like other catalysts, increase the rate of reaction. questions.explanation: Thyroxine, an iodine-containing hormone, is an amino acid, and it is secreted by the thyroid gland. When iodine and thyroxine levels in the blood decrease, secretion of TSH from the pituitary increases. Its effect is to stimulate the thyroid to secrete more and more hormones. Due to iodine deficiency in the body, a disease called goitre occurs.

questions.q: Yeast is used in the production of _____.

questions.explanation: Yeast, mainly Saccharomyces cerevisiae, is used for the production of alcoholic beverages like alcohol and beer because it converts the sugar of grains into ethanol. It is also used in the production of bread. It is also used as a nutritional supplement for humans.

questions.q: Which of the following activities increases oxygen in the carbon cycle occurring on Earth?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

questions.explanation: In the process of photosynthesis, water and carbon dioxide are used and oxygen is released. Therefore, in the carbon cycle on Earth, photosynthesis increases oxygen.

questions.q: During expiration the diaphragm becomes
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The process in which fresh air from the atmosphere reaches our lungs and impure air comes out of the lungs is called breathing (Breathing). This process is completed in two parts— (i) Inhalation (Inspiration), (ii) Exhalation (Expiration). In exhalation (Expiration), carbon dioxide (CO2)-rich air comes out of the lungs. In this, the ribs and diaphragm return to their normal position. The volume of the lungs decreases again. As a result, pressure on the lungs increases and carbon dioxide rich air is expelled from the body. During exhalation, the diaphragm is pulled upward and becomes dome-shaped.

questions.q: During normal respiration in mammals, the diaphragm is-

options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In mammals, during inhalation (inspiration) the diaphragm becomes flattened. In fact, the diaphragm located below the lungs and spreading the thoracic and abdominal cavity is a respiratory muscle in mammals, which helps in the process of breathing.

questions.q: A clinical death takes place when

options.C: Pupils are fixed and dilated and there is no reaction to light
options.D: All the above three conditions are present together
options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Clinical death is not actual death; it means, a person can be revived by CPR or other measures. Clinical death is declared when the following conditions are present together— → Pulse has stopped → Heartbeat has stopped → The pupils are fixed and dilated and show no reaction to light.

questions.q: In how many steps CO2 is released in aerobic respiration?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: During aerobic respiration, carbon dioxide (CO2) is released in three different stages. These stages are as follows— At the time of formation of Acetyl CoA (Acetyl-Coenzyme A), During the Krebs cycle during the conversion of isocitrate to alpha-ketoglutaric acid, and During the Krebs cycle during the conversion of alpha ketoglutarate arale to (Succinyl-CoA).

questions.q: The most important cell type associated with the immunity of the body is
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Lymphocyte is the most important cell type related to the body’s immunity because it is the WBC that secretes the maximum amount of antibody proteins. Lymphocytes are formed in the bone marrow and are found in blood and lymphatic tissues. Lymphocytes are mainly of two types— B-lymphocytes and T-lymphocytes. Notably, in response to pathogens, B-lymphocytes produce a chain of proteins in human blood so that they can fight pathogens. These proteins are called antibodies (Antibodies). T-lymphocytes do not secrete antibodies themselves, but they help Blymphocytes in producing these proteins (antibodies). These are important parts of the immune system, which protect the body from diseases caused by pathogens.

questions.q: Leukemia is a name for several types of cancer that originate in the bone marrow and cause a large number of abnormal blood cells to form. Which blood cell is this?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Leukaemia is a group of blood-related cancers that originate in the bone marrow. In this condition, the number of white blood cells (WBCs) in the blood increases abnormally. WBCs are very important for the body’s immune system, as they protect the body from infections. In leukaemia, the abnormal white blood cells formed are not fully developed, and by crowding out normal blood cell formation, they weaken the body’s immune system.

questions.q: Which one of the following is used in the treatment of blood cancer?

questions.explanation: Radio-phosphorus (P-32) and cobalt-60 are used in the treatment of leukaemia (a type of blood cancer).

questions.q: The total volume of blood in a normal adult human being is
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Blood is a liquid connective tissue. It continuously circulates inside blood vessels through different organs. In humans, the amount of blood is about 7 to 8 percent of body weight. Therefore, in a healthy adult of about 70 kg body weight, there are approximately 5 to 6 litres of blood, which is about one-thirteenth of the total body weight.

questions.q: The function of hemoglobin is -

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Haemoglobin carries oxygen from the lungs to the body tissues and carries carbon dioxide back to the lungs. That is, the function of haemoglobin is to transport oxygen. Oxygen is required for blood circulation and for the functioning of all body organs, in which haemoglobin plays an important role.

questions.q: What prevents backflow of blood during heart contraction?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.B: Thick muscular walls of the ventricles

questions.explanation: During heart contraction, the heart valves prevent the backflow of blood. The atria store blood and their walls are thin. The ventricles pump blood to different parts of the body. Since blood pressure is higher in the ventricles, their walls are thick.

questions.q: In transfusion, blood must be compatible not only in blood type, but also in -
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.D: race of the donor and recipient
options.E: none of the above / more than one of the above

questions.explanation: In blood transfusion, along with the blood group, the Rh factor must also be compatible. The Rh factor was discovered by Landsteiner and Wiener in the blood of the rhesus monkey.

questions.q: Which of the following instrument measures blood pressure –
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: A normal human blood pressure is 120/80 mmHg. There are two stages of blood pressure in arteries. The first is called systolic pressure and the second is called diastolic pressure. Generally, systolic pressure is 120 mmHg and diastolic pressure is 80 mmHg. Doctors measure blood pressure using a sphygmomanometer.

questions.q: In which organ of the human body are the lymphocytes formed?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In the human body, lymphocytes are produced in the spleen, thymus gland, bone marrow, etc. Lymphocytes are a type of white blood cells (WBCs). They move throughout the body like a patrolling force and establish coordination among all parts of the immune system.

questions.q: Which among the following help in circulation of blood?

questions.explanation: Erythrocytes (red blood corpuscles) generally help in the transport of oxygen in blood. Their main function is to carry oxygen from the lungs to all body tissues and to help in transporting apart of carbon dioxide back to the lungs.

questions.q: Blood group of an individual is determined by

questions.q: The universal acceptor blood group is :
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above / more than one of the above

questions.explanation: A person with group O (O–) can donate blood to all groups; therefore, it is called the universal donor. questions.q: The blood group of universal donor is –

questions.q: Defective hemoglobin in the blood is seen in which of the following?

questions.q: Lacteals are associated with which of the following?

options.E: None of the above

questions.q: The most important cell type associated with the body's immune system is -

questions.q: The average blood flow through kidneys per minute is –

questions.explanation: The kidney is an important organ of the human body. Its main function is to purify the blood and remove toxic substances from the body through urine. questions.q: Where is the governing centre of reflex action located?

questions.q: Which of the following glands is called the 'third eye' of the human body?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

questions.q: Hormones are secreted by:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Hormones are chemical messengers of the body, which regulate and coordinate many functions such as growth, metabolism, reproduction, water balance, blood pressure, etc. Hormones are secreted by endocrine glands. questions.q: Which of the following hormones contains iodine?

questions.q: Which of the following is an enhancement of the innate system?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: The autonomic system is a part of the peripheral nervous system. It controls involuntary functions. Therefore, the development of the autonomic system can be defined as the self-regulatory activity.

questions.q: The female sex hormone is :
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above / More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Estrogen is a hormone produced in females by the cells of the theca interna of Graafian follicles in the ovary, from puberty up to the age of menopause (about 45 to 55 years). The main estrogen is estradiol, which is called the female development hormone because it helps in the development of secondary sexual characters (including proper development of breasts, mammary glands, uterus, vagina, etc.) in females.

questions.q: Which of the following rays/waves is used to know the development of the fetus in the womb?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation: To know the development of the fetus in the womb, ultrasonic waves are used in ultrasonography.

questions.q: Sexual reproduction causes genetic variation because of -
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Genetic variation occurs through sexual reproduction due to gene blending, changes in chromosomes, and gene shuffling—all three.

questions.q: Where does fertilization occur?
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: In humans, fertilization is internal. Through sexual intercourse, the male gamete (sperm) enters the female reproductive tract. Sperm are highly active and motile. Millions of sperm enter the vagina and move towards the uterus through the cervix. Finally, only one sperm fertilizes the ovum in the oviduct (fallopian tube).

questions.q: Photosynthesis occurs in-

questions.question_type: Correct Statement — Single Correct

options.B: Energy is released and stored as ATP

questions.q: Plants appear to bend towards light due to–
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.A: Concentration of auxins at shoot tip
options.B: Concentration of auxins at root tip
options.C: Diffusion of auxins towards the shady side of the shoot
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: Auxins are synthesized at the tip of the shoot and help cells to elongate for a longer time. When light falls on the plant from one side, auxin diffuses towards the shaded side of the shoot. The higher auxin concentration on the shaded side stimulates the cells there to elongate more (i. e., on the side away from light). Therefore, the plant appears to bend towards the light.

questions.q: Water passes from the soil into the root by the physical process is called -

questions.q: Where does photosynthesis take place in the cells of a leaf?

questions.q: Which of the following the chlorophyll in photosynthesis is used for ?

In this process, oxygen is released as a by-product. Chlorophyll is a chemical photoreceptor (light-absorbing pigment) that captures light for photosynthesis in plants. It absorbs light mainly in the red (long wavelength) and blue (short wavelength) regions of the visible spectrum. Absorption of green light is very low, and the green light is reflected. That is why a plant appears green.

questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

questions.q: The most important part of the plant in terms of its life cycle is–
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

questions.q: Xylem in plants is responsible for following function:
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.B: Transport of water and dissolved minerals
options.C: Transport of oxygen and other gases

questions.explanation: Xylem is one of the vascular (conducting) tissues of vascular plants. Its main function is to carry the water and dissolved mineral salts absorbed by the roots to the stem, leaves, and other parts of the plant. This transport generally occurs from bottom to top (from root to leaf), so it is considered unidirectional transport.

questions.q: The stomata open or close due to changes in the
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: During the day, due to higher transpiration, water is absorbed by the roots and transported to different parts of the plant through xylem, due to which the guard cells become swollen (turgid). As a result, the stomata open. At night, the guard cells shrink and become rigid because the roots absorb less water; therefore, the stomata close. Potassium plays an important role in the opening and closing of stomata.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a correct match?

questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above / more than one of the above

questions.explanation: The stem helps in distributing food (nutrients) along with water to all parts of the plant and also in storing food (nutrients). It supports the leaves, flowers, and fruits and plays a major role in giving shape to the plant as well.

questions.q: The edible part of litchi is -

questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct

options.E: None of the above

questions.q: What is the movement of the leaves of the sensitive plant Mimosa pudica called?

questions.q: Plants are formed like parent plant from –
questions.question_type: Standard MCQ — Direct Factual/Conceptual, Single Correct
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation is an asexual method of reproduction. In this method, new plants are obtained from parts of old plants (such as stem, root, and leaves) without the involvement of reproductive organs. Stem cutting, layering, and grafting are common methods. New plants produced by asexual reproduction are morphologically and genetically similar to their parent. In contrast, plants produced by sexual reproduction (from seeds) show variations.

questions.q: Embryo is found in –

questions.q: Water-pollinated flowers have pollen grains that are:

questions.q: Among the following, which is not a true fruit?

questions.q: Pollination is best defined as –

questions.q: What is the scientific name of the spice 'Curcuma longa'?

questions.q: Pine, Fir, Spruce, Cedar, Larch and Cypress are the famous timber-yielding plants of which several also occur widely in the hilly regions of India. All these belong to –
